abstract: A white man who had been diagnosed, 35 years previously at the age of 27 months, to have precocious puberty, was later determined to have familial male-limited precocious puberty (FMPP), on the basis of his family history, increased serum testosterone, prepubertal concentrations of follicle stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone, and Leydig cell hyperplasia. Recently, this diagnosis was confirmed by molecular genetic analysis that demonstrated the presence of a heterozygous constitutive activating mutation of the luteinizing hormone/chorionic gonadotropin receptor. This dominant gain-of-function Asp578Gly mutation has been shown constitutively to activate the receptor in the absence of the agonist, leading to enhanced synthesis of cAMP and, in turn, to increased, sustained production of testosterone. In 1994, this patient was found to have a testicular seminoma. He represents the first case of a testicular germ cell tumor described in an FMPP patient, raising the possibility of a potentially harmful effect of prolonged increased concentrations of sex hormones, with onset early in life, upon the cellular components of the testes.
abstract_ja: 35年前、27か月齢時に思春期早発症と診断された白人男性が、家族歴、血清テストステロンの上昇、思春期前のFSHおよびLH濃度、ライディッヒ細胞過形成に基づき、家族性男性限定性思春期早発症（FMPP）と後に判定された。最近の分子遺伝学的解析で、LH/hCG受容体のヘテロ接合性恒常的活性化変異が確認された。このドミナントな機能獲得型変異であるAsp578Glyは、アゴニスト非存在下でも受容体を恒常的に活性化させ、cAMP合成の増加、ひいてはテストステロンの持続的かつ増加した産生を引き起こすことが示されている。1994年、この患者に精巣セミノーマが見つかった。FMPP患者に生じた精巣胚細胞腫瘍の初例であり、早期から始まる性ホルモン濃度の長期的上昇が、精巣の細胞成分に有害に作用する可能性を提起している。
